title: Finish two bounds rules
prompt:
A Range(lo, hi) holds the smallest and largest value a node can have. Each function takes the ranges of the two inputs and returns the range of the answer. Two are nearly done:

  • max_range. The low end is right. The high end says 0. Fill it in.
  • cmplt_range. It returns Range(1, 1) when the compare is always true and Range(0, 1) when it does not know. Add the missing case: return Range(0, 0) when the compare is always false.
hints: Each function has one end right and one case missing. For `max_range`, ask what the largest possible answer is when each input is as large as it can be.
The high end of a max is the larger of the two high ends: `max(a.hi, b.hi)`. The 0 in the starter is a placeholder.

`cmplt_range` already handles always true. The compare is always false when even the smallest `a` is not below the largest `b`: `a.lo >= b.hi`. Only when neither test passes is the answer unknown, `[0, 1]`.
explain: `max` can only raise a value, so each end of the result is the larger of the matching ends, and the high end is `max(a.hi, b.hi)`. A compare is `[1, 1]` when every `a` is below every `b`, which is `a.hi < b.lo`. It is `[0, 0]` when no `a` is below any `b`: `a.lo >= b.hi`. Otherwise it could go either way, `[0, 1]`. This is the rule that turns `cmplt` of a `[0, 7]` value against 8 into `true`.
